relevance_reason: Identifies PAPSS2 loss-of-function mutations as cause of autosomal recessive brachyolmia with variable epiphyseal/metaphyseal changes, the subject of this entry.

findings.statement: Miyake et al. (2012) described 6 patients with autosomal recessive brachyolmia: 3 affected members of a Turkish family, 2 Japanese patients, and 1 Korean patient. The patients had short-trunk short stature that became conspicuous during childhood, with normal intelligence and facies. Radiographic features included rectangular vertebral bodies with irregular endplates and narrow intervertebral discs, precocious calcification of rib cartilages, short femoral neck, and mildly shortened metacarpals; spinal changes were very similar among the 6 patients, whereas epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes of the tubular bones were variable.
quotes: The six patients had short-trunk short stature that became conspicuous during childhood with normal intelligence and facies.

Their radiographic features included rectangular vertebral bodies with irregular endplates and narrow intervertebral discs, precocious calcification of rib cartilages, short femoral neck, and mildly shortened metacarpals.
Spinal changes were very similar among the six patients; however, epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes of the tubular bones were variable.

phenotypes.text: rectangular vertebral bodies with irregular endplates
variable epiphyseal and metaphyseal changes of tubular bones

findings.statement: In 3 affected members of a Turkish family with autosomal recessive brachyolmia, Miyake et al. (2012) used exon capture followed by next-generation sequencing and identified a homozygous loss-of-function mutation in the PAPSS2 gene, c.337_338insG (p.A113GfsX18).
quotes: We examined three affected individuals of the family using exon capture followed by next generation sequencing and identified its disease gene, PAPSS2 (phosphoadenosine-phosphosulfate synthetase 2).
The patients had a homozygous loss of function mutation, c.337_338insG (p.A113GfsX18).

findings.statement: Miyake et al. (2012) identified homozygosity for a PAPSS2 splice mutation, IVS3+2delT, in 1 of 3 additional patients (2 Japanese and 1 Korean) with a similar brachyolmia phenotype.
quotes: We further examined three patients with similar brachyolmia phenotypes (two Japanese and a Korean) and also identified loss of function mutations in PAPSS2; one patient was homozygous for IVS3+2delT

findings.statement: Miyake et al. (2012) identified compound heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in PAPSS2, c.616-634del19 (p.V206SfsX9) and c.1309-1310delAG (p.R437GfsX19), in a patient with brachyolmia (one of 2 Japanese and 1 Korean patients studied).
quotes: the other two were compound heterozygotes for c.616-634del19 (p.V206SfsX9) and c.1309-1310delAG (p.R437GfsX19)

findings.statement: Miyake et al. (2012) identified compound heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in PAPSS2, c.480_481insCGTA (p.K161RfsX6) and c.661delA (p.I221SfsX40), in a patient with brachyolmia (one of 2 Japanese and 1 Korean patients studied).
quotes: c.480_481insCGTA (p.K161RfsX6) and c.661delA (p.I221SfsX40), respectively

findings.statement: Miyake et al. (2012) concluded that PAPSS2 mutations produce a skeletal dysplasia family with a gradation of phenotypes ranging from brachyolmia to spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia.
quotes: PAPSS2 mutations have produced a skeletal dysplasia family, with a gradation of phenotypes ranging from brachyolmia to spondylo-epi-metaphyseal dysplasia.

findings.statement: Miyake et al. (2012) noted that brachyolmia is clinically and genetically heterogeneous, with TRPV4 mutations causing an autosomal dominant form, and identified PAPSS2 as a disease gene for an autosomal recessive form.
quotes: TRPV4 mutations have been identified in an autosomal dominant form of brachyolmia; however, disease genes for autosomal recessive (AR) forms remain totally unknown.
We identified PAPSS2 as the disease gene for an AR brachyolmia.

relevance_reason: Reports a patient with compound heterozygous PAPSS2 mutations and premature pubarche/androgen excess, a feature included in this entry's alternative title (spondylodysplasia and premature pubarche), with functional confirmation.

findings.statement: Noordam et al. (2009) described a girl with premature pubarche, hyperandrogenic anovulation, very low DHEAS levels, and increased androgen levels.
quotes: a girl with premature pubarche, hyperandrogenic anovulation, very low DHEAS levels, and increased androgen levels

findings.statement: In a girl with premature pubarche and androgen excess, Noordam et al. (2009) identified compound heterozygous mutations in the PAPSS2 gene. In vitro coincubation of human SULT2A1 with wild-type or mutant PAPSS2 proteins confirmed that the mutations were inactivating.
quotes: We have identified compound heterozygous mutations in the gene encoding human PAPS synthase 2 (PAPSS2) in a girl with premature pubarche
In vitro coincubation of human SULT2A1 and wild-type or mutant PAPSS2 proteins confirmed the inactivating nature of the mutations.

findings.statement: Noordam et al. (2009) noted that SULT2A1 converts DHEA to its inactive sulfate ester DHEAS, preventing conversion of DHEA to active androgens, and requires PAPS for catalytic activity. They concluded that PAPSS2 deficiency is a monogenic adrenocortical cause of androgen excess.
quotes: SULT2A1 requires 3'-phosphoadenosine-5'-phosphosulfate (PAPS) for catalytic activity.
These observations indicate that PAPSS2 deficiency is a monogenic adrenocortical cause of androgen excess.

relevance_reason: Original report of the Pakistani SEMD family, mapping to 10q23-24, and identification of an ATPSK2 (PAPSS2) nonsense mutation; also the brachymorphic mouse Atpsk2 mutation.

findings.statement: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) studied a large inbred Pakistani family with a distinct form of recessively inherited spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD), a dwarfing condition.
quotes: We have studied a large inbred Pakistani family with a distinct form of recessively inherited spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD)

findings.statement: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) found that SEMD in a large inbred Pakistani family was inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
quotes: We have studied a large inbred Pakistani family with a distinct form of recessively inherited spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD)

findings.statement: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) mapped the gene associated with SEMD in a large inbred Pakistani family to chromosome 10q23-24, a region syntenic with the locus for the brachymorphic mutation on mouse chromosome 19.
quotes: mapped a gene associated with this dwarfing condition to chromosome 10q23-24, a region syntenic with the locus for the brachymorphic mutation on mouse chromosome 19

findings.statement: In affected members of a large inbred Pakistani family with SEMD, Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) identified a nonsense mutation in the ATPSK2 gene, which encodes a novel ATP sulfurylase/APS kinase that catalyzes the activation of inorganic sulfate to PAPS.
quotes: We characterized a nonsense mutation in ATPSK2 in the SEMD family
We identified two orthologous genes, ATPSK2 and Atpsk2, encoding novel ATP sulfurylase/APS kinase orthologues

findings.statement: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) identified a missense mutation in the region of Atpsk2 encoding the APS kinase activity in the brachymorphic mouse, the orthologous locus on mouse chromosome 19.
quotes: a missense mutation in the region of Atpsk2 encoding the APS kinase activity in the brachymorphic mouse

variants.as_reported: missense mutation in the region of Atpsk2 encoding the APS kinase activity

findings.statement: Faiyaz ul Haque et al. (1998) concluded that the cartilage specificity of the human and mouse phenotypes provided evidence of the critical role of sulfate activation to PAPS, the universal donor for protein sulfation, in maturation of cartilage extracellular matrix molecules and skeletogenesis.
quotes: The cartilage-specificity of the human and mouse phenotypes provides further evidence of the critical role of sulfate activation in the maturation of cartilage extracellular matrix molecules

relevance_reason: This is the original description of the Pakistani-type SEMD kindred, which defines this entry.

findings.statement: Ahmad et al. (1998) described a large, inbred, 8-generation kindred from a remote area of Pakistan with a distinct form of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia. They evaluated 16 affected individuals (11 males and 5 females). Clinical findings included short stature evident at birth, short bowed lower limbs, mild brachydactyly, kyphoscoliosis, an abnormal gait, enlarged knee joints, precocious osteoarthropathy, and normal intelligence.
quotes: We describe a large inbred kindred from a remote area of Pakistan, comprising eight generations, with a distinct form of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia (SEMD). We evaluated 16 affected individuals: 11 males and 5 females.

The clinical findings included short stature evident at birth, short bowed lower limbs, mild brachydactyly, kyphoscoliosis, an abnormal gait, enlarged knee joints, precocious osteoarthropathy, and normal intelligence.

findings.statement: Ahmad et al. (1998) reported that radiographs showed delayed epiphyseal ossification at the hips and knees, platyspondyly with irregular end plates and narrowed joint spaces, diffuse early osteoarthritic changes mainly in the spine and hands, and mild brachydactyly. Mild metaphyseal abnormalities were seen mostly at the hips and knees.
quotes: Radiographs demonstrated delayed epiphyseal ossification at the hips and knees, platyspondyly with irregular end plates and narrowed joint spaces, diffuse, early osteoarthritic changes, primarily in the spine and hands, and mild brachydactyly.
Mild metaphyseal abnormalities were seen predominantly at hips and knees.

phenotypes.text: delayed epiphyseal ossification at hips and knees
early osteoarthritic changes in spine and hands
mild metaphyseal abnormalities at hips and knees

findings.statement: Ahmad et al. (1998) concluded that pedigree analysis strongly suggested autosomal recessive inheritance. Consanguineous loops could explain all affected individuals being homozygous for the abnormal allele.
quotes: Analysis of the pedigree strongly suggests autosomal recessive inheritance, and consanguineous loops could account for all the affected individuals being homozygous for the abnormal allele.

findings.statement: Ahmad et al. (1998) concluded that this phenotype is distinct from other autosomal recessive forms of SEMD. They based this on the mild metaphyseal involvement, the type of brachydactyly, and the absence of loose joints or other clinical findings.
quotes: This distinctive phenotype is distinct from other autosomal recessive forms of SEMD because of the mild degree of metaphyseal involvement, the type of brachydactyly, and the absence of loose joints or other clinical findings.
